title: KBL Family gathers veterans to pledge support for Korean basketball
text:
KBL Family gathers veterans to pledge support for Korean basketball - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 11월 1일(일) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English Sports KBL Family gathers veterans to pledge support for Korean basketball 
 입력 2026.10.31. 16:40 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 KBL Family held the 2026-27 general meeting and reunion, taking time for unity to advance Korean basketball.
 KBL Family held the 2026-27 general meeting and reunion on the 28th. The event was attended by key figures in the basketball world, including Kim Dong-gwang, chairman of KBL Family; Kim Dong-wook, former vice chairman of the Korea Basketball Association; Park Geon-yeon, chairman of KXO; Lee Sang-yoon, commentator; Yoon Jeong-no, former president of the mothers' basketball association; and Lee Ho-geun, head coach of Dongguk University.
 At the general meeting, which began with an opening declaration, future activity plans and key matters were shared, followed by the reunion event. In particular, before the main event, a ceremony was held to present sponsorship funds for the development of Korean basketball and KBL Family, adding meaning to the occasion.
 Former professional basketball players Ki Seung-ho and Jo Jae-ho, director of Olbareun Seoul Hospital, delivered donations to support the development of Korean basketball and the activities of KBL Family.
 In his congratulatory remarks, Jo Jae-ho, director of Olbareun Seoul Hospital, said, "I am honored to have an opportunity to do good work for the KBL Family, where the legends of Korean basketball have gathered," and added, "I wish for the continued boundless development of Korean basketball and KBL Family."
 At the subsequent reunion, former Kolon coach Jin Ga-il and elders Yun Jin-gu and Hong Young-soon were celebrated for reaching their 80th and 70th birthdays. Attendees honored the elders who dedicated many years to Korean basketball and shared warm affection.
 In his remarks, Kim Dong-gwang, chairman of KBL Family, said, "We will spare no effort to carry on the traditions KBL Family has achieved so far and to help KBL Family continue to develop."
 The event concluded as a meaningful occasion where people who contributed to the development of Korean basketball gathered in one place to interact, reflect on harmony between seniors and juniors, and reaffirm the traditions of KBL Family.
